\begin{lemma}\label{lem:p142-monotone-parameter-supremum}
Let $Y$ be a topological space, let $c\in\mathbf R$, and, for each
$\tau<c$, let $a_\tau:Y\to[0,+\infty]$ be lower semicontinuous.
Assume that $a_s\leq a_t$ whenever $s\leq t<c$. Then
\[
 F(y):=\sup_{\tau<c}\{\tau-a_\tau(y)\}
 \in[-\infty,c]
\]
is upper semicontinuous. For every dense subset $D\subset(-\infty,c)$,
\begin{equation}
 F(y)=\sup_{\tau\in D}\{\tau-a_\tau(y)\}
 \quad(y\in Y).
 \label{eq:p142-dense-parameter-formula}
\end{equation}
No continuity in $\tau$, countability assumption on $Y$, or finiteness
assumption on $a_\tau(y)$ is required.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:p142-raw-transform-usc}
Let $X$ be a complex manifold, and give the tropical spectrum $X^\beth$
of its coherent ideal sheaves the topology of pointwise convergence on
ideals. Let $c\in\mathbf R$ and let $(\Gamma_\tau)_{\tau<c}$ be a
decreasing family of quasi-plurisubharmonic functions on $X$, none
identically $-\infty$ on a connected component. Put
\begin{equation}
 \nu_v^{\mathcal I}(\Gamma_\tau)
 :=\sup_{m\geq1}\frac1m v\bigl(\mathcal I(m\Gamma_\tau)\bigr),
 \qquad
 F_\Gamma(v):=\sup_{\tau<c}
       \{\tau-\nu_v^{\mathcal I}(\Gamma_\tau)\}.
 \label{eq:p142-raw-transform}
\end{equation}
The supremum defining $\nu_v^{\mathcal I}$ equals the limit as
$m\to\infty$. Then $F_\Gamma$ is upper semicontinuous on all of
$X^\beth$, including semivaluations with nonzero support. Formula
\eqref{eq:p142-dense-parameter-formula} holds for $F_\Gamma$ at every
semivaluation.

More precisely, for $N,M\in\mathbf Z_{>0}$ set
\begin{align}
 \tau_{N,j}&:=c-N+\frac jN \qquad(0\leq j<N^2),
 \label{eq:p142-mesh}\\
 A_{\tau,M}(v)&:=\max_{1\leq m\leq M}
       \frac1m v\bigl(\mathcal I(m\Gamma_\tau)\bigr),
 \label{eq:p142-finite-ideal-values}\\
 B_{N,M}(v)&:=\frac1N+
   \max\left\{c-N,
       \max_{0\leq j<N^2}
        \bigl(\tau_{N,j}-A_{\tau_{N,j},M}(v)\bigr)\right\},
 \label{eq:p142-upper-approximants}\\
 f_k(v)&:=\min_{1\leq N,M\leq k}B_{N,M}(v).
 \label{eq:p142-decreasing-sequence}
\end{align}
Every $B_{N,M}$ and $f_k$ is a bounded, real-valued continuous function
given by a finite expression in negative ideal evaluations $-v(\mathfrak a)$,
real translations, positive rational scaling, minima and maxima. Moreover,
\begin{equation}
 f_k\searrow F_\Gamma\quad\hbox{pointwise on }X^\beth.
 \label{eq:p142-exact-sequential-limit}
\end{equation}
The approximants are not asserted to be MP plurisubharmonic or
semipositive.
\end{theorem}

\begin{corollary}\label{cor:p142-pseudoeffective-raw-usc}
Let $X$ be a connected compact K\"ahler manifold, let $\theta$ be a
smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form with pseudoeffective class, and let
$\boldsymbol\Gamma\in\PSH^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta)$ be a DXZ
inverse-system metric. Its perturbation-independent raw ideal-valuative
transform is upper semicontinuous on $X^\beth$ and has the decreasing
continuous finite-ideal approximation in
\eqref{eq:p142-decreasing-sequence}--\eqref{eq:p142-exact-sequential-limit},
formed from any one perturbation component. Every dense parameter set
computes the same transform at all semivaluations.

This assertion requires neither projectivity nor rationality, bigness,
nefness, or positive volume of the unperturbed class. It asserts no MP
positivity, positive approximation, Monge--Amp\`ere construction, or
identification of $P$-equivalence with $\mathcal I$-equivalence.
\end{corollary}

# Source and scope audit

Date: 2026-08-31. Main author checked the current manuscript, the primary
HTML sources below, and parsed primary PDF text. Web rendering of the DX22
pages returned cache misses, so no visual PDF audit is claimed here.

## Definitional inputs

1. Mesquita-Piccione, arXiv:2409.06221v2, Definition1.3.1:
   <https://arxiv.org/html/2409.06221v2#S1.SS3>.
   The spectrum evaluates coherent ideals in [0,+infinity], with the
   topology of pointwise convergence. Only this definition is needed;
   neither divisorial density nor the dual-complex comparison is used.
2. Darvas--Xia--Zhang, arXiv:2302.02541v3, Section2.2:
   <https://arxiv.org/html/2302.02541v3#S2.SS2>.
   Test-curve levels decrease with the real parameter and have a finite
   terminal parameter. This is the direction of monotonicity needed in
   the finite left-mesh estimate. No continuity of multiplier ideals in
   that parameter is required.
3. The same source, formula(28), Definition3.3, and the paragraph following
   the definition:
   <https://arxiv.org/html/2302.02541v3#S3.SS2>.
   These specify the inverse system, its I-envelope transitions, and its
   common terminal parameter. Preservation of integer multiplier ideals
   is the already established Ch71 transition input; primary item5 below
   supplies its full compact-Kaehler source, rather than deriving it
   solely from the displayed definition.
4. Xia, arXiv:2312.17150v3, Section3.3.2, formula(3.8):
   <https://arxiv.org/html/2312.17150v3#S3.SS3.SSS2>.
   This is a source for the raw multiplier-ideal formula in the smooth
   projective line-bundle setting. Its positivity conclusion is NOT
   imported into the general compact-Kaehler setting.
5. Darvas--Xia, The closures of test configurations and algebraic
   singularity types, Advances in Mathematics397 (2022), 108198:
   <https://research.chalmers.se/publication/528300/file/528300_Fulltext.pdf>.
   Section2.4 explicitly resets its scope to compact Kaehler manifolds
   and pseudoeffective background forms (printed p19). Proposition2.18(ii)
   (printed p22) proves I-equivalence with the I-envelope. The paper's
   ample introductory setup does not narrow this section.
6. Demailly--Ein--Lazarsfeld, A subadditivity property of multiplier ideals:
   <https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~roblaz/Reprints/Demailly.Ein.Laz.Subadditivity.pdf>.
   Theorem2.6(ii) (printed p149) supplies analytic subadditivity on complex
   manifolds. Adding a smooth local function does not change multiplier
   ideals, so the local psh formulation applies to quasi-psh functions.
   That source uses exp(-2 phi), whereas the book uses exp(-phi);
   substituting half the book potential in both source inputs gives
   exactly the subadditivity inclusion used here.

## Existing book inputs

- Ch58, eq:ts-evaluation: topology on all ideal characters, with +infinity.
- Ch71, prop:pseff-ideal-valuative-basic: multiplier-ideal subadditivity
  and the extended-real Fekete formula. The elementary sequence argument
  is repeated in the candidate proof; coherence and subadditivity remain
  the standard complex multiplier-ideal inputs.
- Ch71, thm:pseff-perturbation-independent-transform: exact transition
  ideal equality at every positive integer, usable at every semivaluation.
- Ch72, prob:frontier-mp-pseff and inventory P14.2: the target is USC of
  the raw transform in a general compact-Kaehler pseudoeffective class.

## Newly proved steps requiring review

- A finite left mesh bounds the parameter supremum within its mesh size
  after truncating from below; the negative tail and excluded endpoint
  are both explicitly handled.
- The resulting infimum formula proves USC even where all values are
  minus infinity. Dense-parameter determination uses only monotonicity.
- Truncating the ideal limit at each finite mesh produces continuous
  majorants. Finite running minima over pairs (N,M) give an explicit
  decreasing sequence with the exact raw function as limit.

## Limits

No use of an arbitrary supremum theorem for psh functions, a divisorial
extension theorem, a Gauss identity at nondivisorial points, MP model
nefness, or a positive regularization theorem occurs. In particular the
new sequence must never be cited as settling P14.3. No open atom is retired
until both required verification gates pass.

\begin{example}\label{ex:p142-infinite-ideal-value}
On $X=\mathbf P^1$, choose a point $p$, a smooth Hermitian metric on
$\mathcal O(p)$, and its canonical section $s_p$. Fix $\lambda>0$ and
put $\psi=\lambda\log|s_p|^2$. The family $\Gamma_\tau=\psi$ for
$\tau<c$ satisfies the elementary hypotheses of
\cref{thm:p142-raw-transform-usc}; no assertion that this particular
representative is an $\mathcal I$-model potential is needed.

Writing $\mathfrak m_p$ for the ideal sheaf of $p$, one has
\[
       \mathcal I(m\psi)=\mathfrak m_p^{\lfloor m\lambda\rfloor}.
\]
Indeed, near $p$ a coordinate $z$ expresses $\psi$ as
$\lambda\log|z|^2$ plus a smooth function. A germ of order $q$ is
integrable with the weight $\mathrm e^{-m\psi}$ exactly when
$q-m\lambda>-1$, which is equivalent to $q\geq\lfloor m\lambda\rfloor$.
Away from $p$ the ideal is the unit ideal. It follows that
\[
 \nu_v^{\mathcal I}(\psi)=\lambda v(\mathfrak m_p),
 \qquad F_\Gamma(v)=c-\lambda v(\mathfrak m_p).
\]
At a semivaluation with $v(\mathfrak m_p)=+\infty$, each sufficiently
large multiplier-ideal value is infinite, so the displayed formulas give
$F_\Gamma(v)=-\infty$. For the smaller integers with
$\lfloor m\lambda\rfloor=0$, the ideal is the unit ideal and its value
is zero; no expression $0\cdot(+\infty)$ is used. Thus the infinite-value
case in the theorem records actual support information and cannot be
discarded by restricting to divisorial valuations.
\end{example}

                                                                                         Introduction


                                           The conjecture. The study of algebraic and analytic properties of complex manifolds has
                                           been an active field of research in the area of Kähler Geometry.
                                              To approach many of the questions in this field, one requires generally results and tech-
                                           niques from both Differential and Algebraic Geometry, which shows the connection between
                                           those fields.
                                              One of the most important questions in the area is the Yau–Tian–Donaldson (YTD)
                                           conjecture. It deals with the following question:
                                                                                                   .
                                           Question. Let (X, ω) be a Kähler manifold, and α = [ω] be the cohomology class of ω. Is
                                           there a Kähler metric ω ′ ∈ α, in the same class as ω, such that its scalar curvature
                                                                                           Scal(ω ′ ) ≡ s                                              (0.0.1)
                                           is constant?

                                             This project has received funding from the European Union’s Horizon 2020 research and innovation
                                           programme under the Marie Sklodowska-Curie grant agreement No 945332.
                                                                                                  1
 2                                         P. MESQUITA-PICCIONE

   When X is a Fano variety, i.e. X is anticanonically polarized, Chen–Donaldson–Sun
[CDS15a, CDS15b, CDS15c] and Tian [Tia15] showed, using the continuity method, that
X admits a constant scalar curvature Kähler metric (cscK metric) if, and only if, X is
K-stable. Later other proofs became available, like [BBJ21], [Szé16, DS16], [CSW18], and
[DZ24] among others.
   K-stability is an algebro-geometric notion that deals with the study of 1-parameter degen-
erations of the manifold X, together with a numerical invariant. This notion is an infinite
dimensional analogue of stability in the sense of Geomtric Invariant Theory (GIT). In that
context, by the Kempf–Ness Theorem, studying the stability of an orbit of a hamiltonian
group action is equivalent to finding zeros of an associated moment map.
   The general –still open– version of the Yau–Tian–Donaldson conjecture reads:
Conjecture (YTD Conjecture). There exists a unique constant scalar curvature Kähler
(cscK) metric in α if, and only if, (X, α) is uniformly K-stable in the sense of [SD18, DR17b].


A variational approach. The PDE of equation (0.0.1) has a variational interpretation
that will play the key role in our approach to the YTD Conjecture. This approach was
developed by many authors, see [BB17], [BBE+ 19], [Che00], [Dar15], and [DR17a] for some
important work. We describe this approach now.
   By the ∂∂-lemma, if ω ′ ∈ α is a Kähler metric in the cohomology class of ω, then
 ′
ω − ω = ddc u, for u : X → R a smooth function satisfying:
                                              ω + ddc u > 0.
We denote ω ′ by ωu , and we call u a potential of ω ′ . In these terms, Equation (0.0.1)
translates to a fourth order elliptic PDE on the potential.
   The space of the potentials, in a given class [ω], is denoted by
                          .  
                    H(ω) = u : X → R u smooth, and ω + ddc u > 0 .
   In order to have a good geometric setting to carry out the variational calculus for studying
this PDE, we must consider a completion1 of H(ω), the space E 1 (ω).
   By the groundbreaking work of Chen–Cheng [CC21a, CC21b], we know that there exists
a unique solution for (0.0.1) if and only if a given functional, called the Mabuchi functional,
Mω : E 1 (ω) → R, satisfies:
                                              Mω ≥ δJω − C,                              (0.0.2)
for some C, δ > 0, and where Jω is a “norm like” functional. If it is the case, Mω is said to
be coercive.
   In this setting the YTD conjecture can be stated as follows:
Conjecture (YTD Conjectrue). The Mabuchi functional is coercive if, and only if, (X, α)
is uniformly K-stable in the sense of [SD18, DR17b].
Remark 0.0.1. When X is a Kähler variety of klt singularities either Q-Gorenstein smooth-
able, or admitting a resolution of singularities of nef relative anticanonical bundle, by [PTT23]
in the first case, and combining works of [BJT24, PT24] in the second case, we have that
the coercivity of the Mabuchi functional implies the existence of a positive closed current in
α, that is a cscK metric on the regular locus, and has bounded potential. In this generality,
the above conjecture is completely open.

    1for the Darvas metric d , see [Dar15].

          A NON-ARCHIMEDEAN THEORY OF COMPLEX SPACES AND THE CSCK PROBLEM                                     3

Varional approach in the Fano setting. In the Fano case, Berman–Boucksom–Jonsson, in
[BBJ21], used the variational approach to prove the conjecture. Their proof relied on two
observations:
      • It was already known, in the Fano case, that the existence of a cscK metric is
          equivalent to the coercivity of a different –and simpler– functional defined on the
          space of potentials D : E 1 (ω) → R, the Ding functional.
      • By [BHJ17], there is a non-Archimedean description of K-stability: there is a non-
          Archimedean counterpart of H(ω) on the Berkovich analytification of X, X an , de-
          noted HNA , in which we can define a non-Archimedean analogue of the Ding func-
          tional, DNA : HNA → R, and K-stability becomes equivalent to the coercivity of this
          functional.
   Thus, using the simpler analysis of the Ding functional, Berman–Boucksom–Jonsson
proved that the slope formulas for psh rays of algebraic singularities guarantee the coer-
civity of the functional D, as soon as one supposes the coercivity of the non-Archimedean
counterpart DNA .
   In the general case the conjecture is still open, [SD18] and [DR17b] independetly proved
–in the Kähler case– one direction of the conjecture: the coercivity of the Mabuchi functional
implies uniform K-stability.
   The best result in the reciprocal direction is due Chi Li: in [Li22], he adapted the strategy
of Berman–Boucksom–Jonsson to the Mabuchi functional, getting a weaker form of the open
direction of the YTD conjecture for projective manifolds, i.e. he proved that stronger version
of K-stability implies the coercivity of the Mabuchi functional.
   The key ingredient in Chi Li’s paper consists of proving that a distabilizing ray, a ray of
functions that contradicts the coercivity of the Mabuchi functional Mω , must be a maximal
geodesic ray, that is, it must come from a non-Archimedean potential of finite energy: Like
for H(ω), the set of potentials of finite energy E 1 (ω) also has a non-Archimedean counterpart,
E 1,NA , and there is a correspondence between such potentials of finite energy and maximal
geodesic rays, a disguished class of rays in E 1 (ω). Having this in hand, he uses the finer
slope formulas for maximal rays, and then the strategy of [BBJ21] follows in this general
polarized case.
   The goal of this paper is to generalize this result of Chi Li to the transcendental setting.
We prove:
Theorem A. Let (X, α) be a compact Kähler manifold that is uniformly K-stable over E 1 .
Then, α contains a unique cscK metric.

General strategy and main results. By the work of Sjöström Dyrefelt and Dervan–Ross,
there exists a theory of K-stability for Kähler manifolds, but in order to adapt the strategy
of Chi Li –or ultimately of BBJ–, one needs a non-Archimedean theory for a transcendental
complex manifold, where the language of K-stability can be translated to.
   We hence start by developing this non-Archimedean theory. More precisely, we associate
to a complex manifold, X, a “non-Archimedean” compact Hausdorff topological space of
semivaluations on X, defined as the tropical spectrum of the set of coherent ideals of X,
which we denote by X ℶ . This notion coincides with the Berkovich analytification of X
whenever the latter is a proper algebraic variety2, and moreover it also has a description as
the limit of a Dual Complex, just like in algebraic setting.
   2We recall that if X is a proper scheme over a trivially valued field, its Berkovich analytification X an is
defined as the set of all valuations v : C(Y )∗ → R, for Y ⊆ X a subvariety, and C(Y ) its function field. When
X is a compact complex manifold, we may have that its function field is trivial, and moreover it may not
have any non-trivial subvarieties. We cannot use this approach to define X ℶ .
 4                                   P. MESQUITA-PICCIONE

  The most important class of semivaluations is the one of the divisorial valuations, which
are given by
                                  OX ⊇ I 7→ ordF (I · OY )
for F ⊆ Y → X a smooth irreducible reduced divisor on a normal model of X. The next
main theorem we prove establishes the density of the set of divisorial valuations, X div , on
X ℶ.
Theorem B. X div is dense in X ℶ .
   The proof of Theorem B crucially requires a description of the divisorial valuations of X
as the C∗ -invariant divisorial valuations on X × P1 . We get this description by studying the
divisorial valuations on “local algebraic models” of X, that is, for each p ∈ X, we study the
                                          .
divisorial valuations of the scheme Xp = Spec OX,p .
   After establishing some first basic results, we develop a non-Archimedean pluripoten-
tial theory for X ℶ , key for the non-Archimedean approach of [BBJ21]. We define non-
Archimedean psh functions, and a mixed energy coupling, that allow us to:
    (1) Use the synthetic pluripotential theory of [BJ25].
    (2) Define non-Archimedean versions of classical functionals like: the Monge–Ampère
        energy; the twisted energy; the entropy; and finally the J functional.
We then denote by E 1 (α) the set of non-Archimedean potentials of finite Monge–Ampère
energy.
   In the algebraic setting this theory coincides with the one of [BJ22]. In the transcendental
setting Darvas–Xia–Zhang develop a non-Archimedean pluripotential theory for a big class,
on [DXZ25], that coincides with ours on a Kähler class. Their non-Archimedean pluripoten-
tial theory is not over a “non-Archimedean space”, and hence ours is a more direct analogue
of the algebraic theory. In particular, we can make sense of Monge–Ampère equations in
our case, while it is not clear how to interpret them in their formalism.
   Like in [BBJ21], we have that the pluripotential theory developed here behaves well with
the complex one: to each psh ray of potentials Ut we have associated a non-Archimedean psh
function U ℶ . Reciprocally, to each non-Archimedean psh function of finite energy φ ∈ E 1 (α),
there exists a psh ray Vt such that V ℶ = φ. Moreover, there exists a 1to1 correspondence
between maximal geodesic rays in E 1 (ω) and non-Archimedean potentials in E 1 (α). This is
the basis of the correspondence with the theory of [DXZ25].
   For maximal geodesic rays we get formulas of the type:
                                          F(Us )
                                    lim          = Fℶ (U ℶ ),                           (0.0.3)
                                   s→∞      s
for F either E, Eη , or J, and an inequality for the entropy:
                                         Hω (Us )
                                   lim            ≥ Hα (U ℶ ).                          (0.0.4)
                                            s
Adding all together we get:
                                        Mω (Us )
                                   lim            ≥ Mα (U ℶ ),
                                   s→∞      s
where Mα is the non-Archimedean Mabuchi functional, the non-Archimedean counterpart of
Mω providing the good inequality to conclude the proof of Theorem A.
  Indeed, just like in the projective setting, if Mω is not coercive we can find a geodesic ray
Ut ∈ E 1 such that t 7→ Mω (Ut ) is decreasing for t large. We call such a ray a destabilizing
geodesic ray.
         A NON-ARCHIMEDEAN THEORY OF COMPLEX SPACES AND THE CSCK PROBLEM                      5

  Analogously to [Li22], every destabilizing ray is maximal, that is, it is a geodesic ray
coming from a non-Archimedean potential of finite energy, φ ∈ E 1 (α). In particular:
                                       Mω (Ut )
                                    lim         ≥ Mα (φ).                           (0.0.5)
                                    t→∞   t
  Like this, we prove that if (X, ω) is such that Mα : E 1 (α) → R is positive, then there
exists a unique cscK metric on α, proving Theorem A.

The YTD conjecture and Chi Li’s result. In the non-Archimedean terms of the present
paper K-stability reads as the coercivity of the non-Archimedean Mabuchi functional:
Definition 0.0.2. The pair (X, α) is uniformly K-stable if there exists a δ > 0 such that
                                       Mα (φ) ≥ δJα (φ)
for every φ ∈ H(α), that is if Mα is coercive over H(α).
  In this paper, we have proved that a stronger version of K-stability, uniform K-stability
over E 1 (α), implies the coercivity of the K-energy, and hence the existence of a unique cscK
metric. In order to prove the conjecture one would need to prove that
                      Mα |H(α) ≥ δJα |H(α) =⇒ Mα |E 1 (α) ≥ δ ′ Jα |E 1 (α) ,
for some δ, δ ′ > 0.
   In [Li22], Chi Li proves that, in the projective case, one has
                Mα |C0 ∩ PSH(α) ≥ δJα |C0 ∩ PSH(α) =⇒ Mα |E 1 (α) ≥ δJα |E 1 (α) ,
obtaining that an intermediate version of K-stability implies the coercivity of the K-energy.
   In this paper we not able to get a sharper result, like this one of Chi Li, in the tran-
scendental setting. His result relies on the solution of the non-Archimedean Monge–Ampère
equation of [BFJ15] that we don’t have at our disposal.
Remark 0.0.3. We would like to note that in an upcoming work of David Witt Nyström
together with the author [MPN25], they are able to establish the analogue of [BFJ15] in the
setting of the present paper. They solve the non-Archimedean Monge–Ampère equation for
non-algebraic Kähler manifolds and, in particular, prove that the intermediate notion of
uniform K-stability of Chi Li implies uniform K-stability over E 1 . This recovers Chi Li’s
result in the projective setting. Moreover, this forthcoming work provides a new valuative
criterion for K-stability over E 1 .
  Furthermore, in the same paper Chi Li also gives a version of his theorem when X admits
automorphisms, which we don’t treat in present paper.
Organization of the paper.
    • In Section 1 we define our “non-Archimedean analytification” of a locally ringed
      space, we do some basic constructions and we compare it to Berkovich analytification
      of a scheme.
    • Section 2 deals with the study of X ℶ , when X is a normal compact complex space.
      We prove Theorem B, getting a theory which resembles closely the one of the
      Berkovich analytification of a projective variety over C.
    • Section 3 contains a dual complex description of X ℶ , analogue to the one found in
      [BJ22].
    • Section 4 is devoted to developing the non-Archimedean pluripotential theory of X ℶ .
    • In Section 5 we compare the pluripotential theory of X ℶ with the transcendental
      non-Archimedean theory of [DXZ25, Xia25] , and get slope formulas, generalizing
      the results of [SD18, DR17b, Li22].
 6                                    P. MESQUITA-PICCIONE

     • In Section 6 we define strong K-stability, and prove Theorem A, the main result of
       the paper.

                               Notations and Conventions
   Through out this paper, a ring will always be unital and commutative. By an analytic
variety we mean a reduced and irreducible complex analytic space. Given X an analytic
variety we denote by X e the normalization of X, cf. [GR12, Chapter 6]. Moreover, we simply
call ideal a coherent ideal sheaf of OX . We call flag ideal a C∗ -invariant fractional coherent
ideal of OX×P1 , supported on X × {0}, and we denote the set of such ideals by F .
   A flag ideal a ∈ F can be written as a sum:
                                             X
                                         a=      aλ tλ ,                                  (0.0.6)
                                               λ∈Z

for (aλ )λ an increasing sequence of ideals of X such that aλ = 0 for λ ≪ 0 and aλ = OX for
λ ≫ 0.
   An ideal on X will typically be denoted by I, J or K. An ideal on X × P1 will typically
be denoted either a or b.
   An ideal I on X is a prime ideal if given J, K ideals on X satisfying:
                                           I ⊇ J · K,

                                                A transcendental approach to non-Archimedean
                                                       metrics of pseudoeffective classes
                                                          Tamás Darvas, Mingchen Xia and Kewei Zhang


                                                                                    Abstract




arXiv:2302.02541v3 [math.AG] 17 Jul 2024
                                                    We introduce the concept of non-Archimedean metrics attached to a transcen-
                                                dental pseudoeffective cohomology class on a compact Kähler manifold. This is
                                                obtained via extending the Ross–Witt Nyström correspondence to the relative case,
                                                and we point out that our construction agrees with that of Boucksom–Jonsson when
                                                the class is induced by a pseudoeffective Q-line bundle.
                                                    We introduce the notion of a flag configuration attached to a transcendental big
                                                class, recovering the notion of a test configuration in the ample case. We show that
                                                non-Archimedean finite energy metrics are approximable by flag configurations, and
                                                very general versions of the radial Ding energy are continuous, a novel result even
                                                in the ample case. As applications, we characterize the delta invariant as the Ding
                                                semistability threshold of flag configurations and filtrations, and prove a YTD type
                                                existence theorem for Kähler–Einstein metrics in terms of flag configurations.

 1    Introduction and results
In recent years, especially since the appearance of [BBJ21], the non-Archimedean ap-
proach to K-stability has gained attention, as evidenced by recent works [BJ21; BE21;
BHJ17; BJ18; DL20b; Li20; BJ22b], to name only a few papers in the fast expanding
literature.
    Studying K-stability for degenerate classes is a natural extension of the much studied
ample case [CDS15; DS16; Tia15; TW20; CSW18; BBJ21; Zha21]. Recent works aim
to understand existence of canonical metrics in this context as well. Degenerate Kähler–
Einstein metrics have taken the forefront [LTW21a; LTW21b; LXZ22; DZ22; DR22;
Xu22], but one would think that the notion of constant scalar curvature Kähler metrics
also extends to big classes, as minimzers of the K-energy functional. With the study still
in its infancy [Zhe22; DL22], a better understanding of K-stability of big classes is needed
before substantial progress can be made. Our work tries to fill some of this void.
    We propose a transcendental approach to non-Archimedean metrics, that allows for
their treatment even for a transcendental pseudoeffective class. Our analytic treatment
has a number of advantages. The envelope conjecture of Boucksom–Jonsson naturally
holds in our context, immediately recovering the main result of [BJ22a], as a particular
case. We show that very general versions of the radial Ding energy are continuous, and
that finite energy non-Archimedean metrics can be approximated by algebraic objects
called flag configurations (that reduce to test configurations in the ample case). The
latter two properties allow to characterize the analytically defined delta invariant using
algebraic data, and provide a YTD type existence theorem for big Kähler–Einstein (KE)
metrics, without using the minimal model program, connecting with recent work of the
first and third authors [DZ22].

Transcendental non-Archimedean metrics. To state our main results, we fix some
terminology. Let X be a compact Kähler manifold and θ a smooth closed real (1, 1)-form
representing a pseudoeffective cohomology class {θ}. We denote by PSH(X, θ) the space
of θ-psh functions, and all complex Monge–Ampère measures in this work will be assumed
to be pluripolar in the sense of [BEGZ10].

{ψτ }τ is a test curve relative to ψ−∞ .

be a (partial) flag of coherent analytic ideal sheaves

By convention, aℓ := 0 for ℓ ∈ Z<0 and aℓ := aN if ℓ ∈ Z≥N . A flag configuration will be

where s denotes the coordinate on C = Spec C[s]. In this transcendental big setting,

    As we point out in (47), in case {θ} is the first Chern class of a big line bundle L, to

that even in the big case, one can associate a natural geodesic ray/maximal test curve to

flag configurations or filtrations, extending [DX22, Theorem 1.1] to the big case, making

the study of the non-Archimedean Monge–Ampère measures. The pluripotential
theory on non-Archimedean curves was developed in detail in the thesis of Thuillier
[Thu05]. All these developments together lead to the natural question: To what
extent is there a pluripotential theory on Berkovich spaces similar to its complex
counterpart?
    This question has drawn the attention of many authors. In particular, so far
we know that there are two general approaches in the literature.
    The first approach is the local approach, initiated by Chambert-Loir–Ducros
[CLD12] and Gubler [Gub16]. In this approach, one defines the notions of dif-
ferential forms and currents on a Berkovich space based on local tropicalizations.
Then one can define the Monge–Ampère operator using the usual differential for-
mula. The problem is that this approach only works for regular plurisubharmonic
functions and completely fails when a singularity is presented. This is an essential
obstacle for applications to complex geometry.
    The second approach was initiated by Boucksom–Favre–Jonsson in [BFJ15,
BFJ16], following the original ideas of Zhang. In the trivially valued case, this
theory was further developed by Boucksom–Jonsson [BJ22a]. In this approach,
one first considers metrics obtained from semipositive models and then defines gen-
eral global plurisubharmonic metrics using approximations. This approach allows
singularities but does not work in the local situation. It does not yield a sheaf of
plurisubharmonic metrics. Both approaches have their own drawbacks. We do not
have a completely satisfactory non-Archimedean pluripotential theory yet.



      1.2. The transcendental theory. The non-Archimedean pluripotential the-
ory is closely related to complex geometry. We refer to [BBJ21] and the references
therein. The basic idea is that the degeneration in the space of Kähler potentials can
be characterized using global plurisubharmonic metrics on the non-Archimedean
space. This idea has been intensively studied in [BBJ21, Li22, DX21, Xia23].
      We observe that there is a strong obstacle in applying the non-Archimedean
geometry to complex geometry: The envelope conjecture [BJ22a, Conjecture 5.14]
of Boucksom–Jonsson remains open. This conjecture together with its various
consequences is indispensable for various applications.
      In our previous work [DXZ23], we introduced a different framework for the
non-Archimedean global pluripotential theory based on the series of works start-
ing from [BBJ21, RWN14]. Roughly speaking, we represent a non-Archimedean
metric in PSHNA (X, θ) by a test curve Γ = (Γτ )τ , a concave curve of I-model po-
tentials. Due to the pathology caused by zero-mass, the rigorous definition requires
a projective limit construction as well, we refer to Definition 3.5 for the rigorous
definition. In this short introduction, we will only talk about test curves to simplify
our presentation.
      In the algebraic setting, when Boucksom–Jonsson’s theory is applicable, there
is an obvious comparison map sending Γ to a function on the non-Archimedean
space. See Definition 3.11 for the details. The main result in [DXZ23] asserts
that when X is smooth, this comparison map is in fact a bijection to Boucksom–
Jonsson’s theory, hence giving a complex representation of the non-Archimedean
pluripotential theory. When X is only unibranch, Boucksom–Jonsson’s theory is
still applicable. In this case, we prove the following result:

    Theorem 1.1 (=Corollary 5.3). Assume that X is a reduced irreducible uni-
branch projective variety over C and L is a pseudoeffective line bundle on X. Then
the following are equivalent:
      (1) Boucksom–Jonsson’s envelope conjecture holds for (X, L);
      (2) The comparison map extends to a bijection from the space of non-Archi-
          medean potentials in the sense of [DXZ23] to the corresponding space in
          the sense of [BJ22a].

is smooth, as confirmed in [BJ22b]. A different proof was given in [DXZ23].

theoretic operations in Boucksom–Jonsson’s theory to our transcendental theory.

   A major theme in Kähler geometry is to relate algebraic objects to analytic ones.
In this work we address two such problems. First, we give cohomological and potential
theoretic characterizations for L1 geodesic rays in the space of Kähler metrics that lie

problems at the same time, with our ﬁnal answers also paralleling each other on many
diﬀerent levels. We now present one facet of this, with slight abuse of precision.

Detecting singularities using algebraic tools. In this section, let (X, ω) be a compact
Kähler manifold of dimension n. Let θ be a smooth real (1, 1)-form on X representing a
pseudo-eﬀective cohomology class.

one can not characterize the singularity type [u] using “mainstream” algebraic data, like
multiplier ideal sheaves I(cu), c > 0 or Lelong numbers. Instead, one can introduce an
algebraic notion that is coarser than equivalence up to singularity types, considered in

                                                                                     Introduction

                                                   The purpose of this note is to establish a “subadditivity” theorem for multiplier
                                             ideals. As an application, we give a new proof of a theorem of Fujita concerning the
                                             volume of a big line bundle.
                                                  Let X be a smooth complex quasi-projective variety, and let D be an effective
                                             Q-divisor on X. One can associate to D its multiplier ideal sheaf
                                                                                J (D) = J (X, D) ⊆ OX ,
                                             whose zeroes are supported on the locus at which the pair (X, D) fails to have log-terminal
                                             singularities. It is useful to think of J (D) as reflecting in a somewhat subtle way the
                                             singularities of D: the “worse” the singularities, the smaller the ideal. These ideals and
                                             their variants have come to play an increasingly important role in higher dimensional
                                             geometry, largely because of their strong vanishing properties. Among the papers in
                                             which they figure prominently, we might mention for instance [30], [4], [33], [2], [13], [34],
                                             [19], [14] and [8]. See [6] for a survey.
                                                  We establish the following “subadditivity” property of these ideals:
                                             Theorem. Given any two effective Q-divisors D1 and D2 on X, one has the relation
                                                                           J (D1 + D2 ) ⊆ J (D1 ) · J (D2 ).

                                             The Theorem admits several variants. In the local setting, one can associate a multiplier
                                             ideal J (a) to any ideal a ⊆ OX , which in effect measures the singularities of the divisor
                                             of a general element of a. Then the statement becomes
                                                                                J (a · b) ⊆ J (a) · J (b).
                                             On the other hand, suppose that X is a smooth projective variety, and L is a big line
                                             bundle on X. Then one can define an “asymptotic multiplier ideal” J (kLk) ⊆ OX , which
                                             reflects the asymptotic behavior of the base-loci of the linear series |kL| for large k. In
                                             this setting the Theorem shows that
                                                                                J (kmLk) ⊆ J (kLk) m .

\begin{proof}[Proof of \cref{lem:p142-monotone-parameter-supremum}]
For $N\geq1$ put $a=c-N$, and partition $[a,c)$ into the $N^2$
half-open intervals
\[
 [\tau_{N,j},\tau_{N,j}+1/N),\qquad
 \tau_{N,j}=c-N+j/N,\quad 0\leq j<N^2.
\]
Only left endpoints are sampled; the family is never evaluated at $c$.
Set
\[
 F_N:=\max\{c-N,F\},\qquad
 G_N:=\max\left\{c-N,
      \max_{0\leq j<N^2}
       (\tau_{N,j}-a_{\tau_{N,j}})\right\}.
\]
Every sampled term occurs in the supremum defining $F$, so $G_N\leq F_N$.
If $\tau<c-N$, nonnegativity gives $\tau-a_\tau\leq c-N$.
Otherwise there is $j$ with
$\tau_{N,j}\leq\tau<\tau_{N,j}+1/N$. Monotonicity in the parameter
gives, in extended-real order,
\[
 \tau-a_\tau
 \leq \tau-a_{\tau_{N,j}}
 \leq \tau_{N,j}-a_{\tau_{N,j}}+1/N
 \leq G_N+1/N.
\]
This also holds when one or both of the ideal-type quantities are infinite:
only a finite real number minus $+\infty$ occurs. Taking the supremum and
including the floor proves
\begin{equation}
             G_N\leq F_N\leq G_N+1/N.
 \label{eq:p142-grid-sandwich}
\end{equation}

Each $G_N$ is a finite-valued upper-semicontinuous function, since
$-a_{\tau_{N,j}}$ is upper semicontinuous. The sandwich gives the exact
identity
\begin{equation}
                  F=\inf_{N\geq1}(G_N+1/N).
 \label{eq:p142-usc-infimum}
\end{equation}
Indeed, $F\leq F_N\leq G_N+1/N$, and
$G_N+1/N\leq F_N+1/N$ tends pointwise to $F$ as $N\to\infty$.
If $F(y)=-\infty$, then $F_N(y)=c-N$, so the same conclusion holds
at that point. An arbitrary infimum of upper-semicontinuous functions is
upper semicontinuous: its strict sublevel set is the union of the strict
sublevel sets of its terms. This proves the first assertion on an
arbitrary topological space.

For the dense-parameter assertion, fix $y$ and $\tau<c$ with
$a_\tau(y)<+\infty$. Given $\varepsilon>0$, choose
$s\in D\cap(\tau-\varepsilon,\tau)$. Then
\[
 s-a_s(y)\geq s-a_\tau(y)
              >\tau-a_\tau(y)-\varepsilon.
\]
Thus the supremum over $D$ is at least every finite term in the full
supremum, after letting $\varepsilon$ tend to zero. Terms equal to
$-\infty$ impose no further condition. If all terms are $-\infty$,
both suprema are $-\infty$. The opposite inequality follows from
$D\subset(-\infty,c)$, proving
\eqref{eq:p142-dense-parameter-formula}.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}[Proof of \cref{thm:p142-raw-transform-usc}]
Multiplier ideal sheaves of quasi-psh functions on a complex manifold
are coherent. Their subadditivity \cite[Theorem~2.6(ii)]{DEL00} gives
\[
 \mathcal I((m+\ell)\Gamma_\tau)
 \subseteq\mathcal I(m\Gamma_\tau)
               \mathcal I(\ell\Gamma_\tau).
\]
Ideal values reverse inclusion and add under multiplication. Hence
$b_m=v(\mathcal I(m\Gamma_\tau))$ is a nonnegative extended-real
superadditive sequence. If some $b_q=+\infty$, superadditivity implies
$b_m=+\infty$ for every $m\geq q$: use $m=q+r$ for $r\geq1$.
Otherwise, for a fixed $q$, writing $m=kq+r$, with $0\leq r<q$, gives
$b_m\geq kb_q$ (put $b_0=0$). Therefore
\[
 \liminf_{m\to\infty}\frac{b_m}{m}\geq\frac{b_q}{q}.
\]
Taking the supremum over $q$ and comparing with the immediate upper
bound proves the limit assertion, including an infinite supremum. This
is the multiplier-ideal argument recorded in
\cref{prop:pseff-ideal-valuative-basic}.

By the topology of the tropical spectrum, the function
$v\mapsto v(\mathfrak a)$ is continuous into $[0,+\infty]$ with its
order topology for every coherent ideal $\mathfrak a$; see
\cite[Definition~1.3.1]{MP24} and \eqref{eq:ts-evaluation}.
It follows that
\[
 v\longmapsto\nu_v^{\mathcal I}(\Gamma_\tau)
   =\sup_{m\geq1}\frac1m
          v(\mathcal I(m\Gamma_\tau))
\]
is lower semicontinuous. If $s\leq t<c$, then
$\Gamma_s\geq\Gamma_t$. Local integrability immediately implies
\[
 \mathcal I(m\Gamma_t)\subseteq\mathcal I(m\Gamma_s),
 \qquad
 \nu_v^{\mathcal I}(\Gamma_s)
       \leq\nu_v^{\mathcal I}(\Gamma_t).
\]
For the first inclusion, multiplication of the weight by the bounded
factor associated to an additive local constant would also suffice;
the given pointwise order already yields it directly. No assertion
about continuity of multiplier ideals in the parameter is used.
The hypotheses of \cref{lem:p142-monotone-parameter-supremum} are now
verified, and that lemma proves upper semicontinuity and the dense-set
formula at every semivaluation.

We prove the stronger explicit approximation assertion separately.
For fixed $N,M$, all ideal evaluations in
\eqref{eq:p142-upper-approximants} are continuous extended-real
functions. Their displayed finite maxima and positive scalings are
continuous in the order topology; subtracting from the finite
$\tau_{N,j}$ gives a continuous function into $[-\infty,\tau_{N,j}]$.
The outer maximum with $c-N$ then yields an ordinary real-valued
continuous function. In particular,
\[
        c-N+1/N\leq B_{N,M}\leq c+1/N.
\]
This establishes boundedness without invoking compactness of $X^\beth$.

As $M$ increases, $A_{\tau,M}\nearrow\nu^{\mathcal I}(\Gamma_\tau)$.
For the finite number of sampled parameters, taking the maximum commutes
with these decreasing limits after changing the sign. To see this even
at $-\infty$, if every limiting term is below a chosen real threshold,
then every term is eventually below it; a maximum of finitely many
indices works for all terms. The fixed finite floor is retained throughout.
Consequently, with $G_N$ as in the preceding proof,
\[
           B_{N,M}\searrow G_N+1/N\quad(M\to\infty).
\]
The sandwich \eqref{eq:p142-grid-sandwich} gives
\begin{equation}
 F_\Gamma\leq B_{N,M},\qquad
 \inf_{N,M\geq1}B_{N,M}
      =\inf_{N\geq1}(G_N+1/N)=F_\Gamma.
 \label{eq:p142-double-infimum}
\end{equation}
Every $f_k$ is a finite minimum of bounded continuous real-valued
functions. The squares $\{1,\ldots,k\}^2$ increase and exhaust
$\mathbf Z_{>0}^2$, so their minima decrease to the double infimum
in \eqref{eq:p142-double-infimum}. This is
\eqref{eq:p142-exact-sequential-limit}.

The construction is explicit. It does not extract a sequence from an
arbitrary net on a nonmetrizable space. Nor does a minimum of these
continuous functions acquire a positivity property merely because it
is formed from ideal values. No positive approximation is asserted.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}[Proof of \cref{cor:p142-pseudoeffective-raw-usc}]
Fix one K\"ahler perturbation component
$\Gamma=(\Gamma^{\theta+\omega}_\tau)_{\tau<c}$, where
$c=\boldsymbol\Gamma_{\max}$. The DXZ test-curve definition supplies
a decreasing family of quasi-psh functions with finite terminal
parameter, and its interior levels are not identically $-\infty$;
see \cite[Section~2.2, Definition~3.3]{DXZ23}.
\Cref{thm:p142-raw-transform-usc} therefore applies to this component.

The identification with the raw inverse-system transform uses only the
already established transition identity, not an MP comparison theorem.
Under a transition the interior level is replaced by its
$\mathcal I$-model envelope in the larger class. This preserves every
integer multiplier ideal by \cite[Proposition~2.18(ii)]{DX22}; the
standing hypotheses of its Section~2.4 allow an arbitrary compact
K\"ahler manifold and a pseudoeffective background class. A common
dominating component compares any
two choices, and their terminal parameters coincide. Evaluating those
same ideals at any semivaluation proves that both the raw transform and
the explicit expressions \eqref{eq:p142-finite-ideal-values}--
\eqref{eq:p142-decreasing-sequence} are unchanged. These are precisely
the ideal equalities in
\cref{thm:pseff-perturbation-independent-transform}; the source
transition is \cite[formula~(28), Definition~3.3]{DXZ23}.

All arguments take place on a perturbed component. No potential of
positive mass in the unperturbed class is chosen, so zero-volume
pseudoeffective classes are included. The proof does not construct
relatively nef cohomological models, a Monge--Amp\`ere operator, or an
energy. Those are distinct questions.
\end{proof}
